name: Southeast Brazil (São Paulo · Rio · Minas Gerais)

language.script_notes: Brazilian Portuguese, identical to the national profile — ã, õ, ç, -ção endings, black-backed direction signs, BR-XXX highway shields. Route numbers 1–2 sit around São Paulo and Rio, so low BR numbers point here.

road_furniture.bollard_color: No standard bollard, as elsewhere in Brazil.
road_furniture.guardrail_type: Steel W-beam on rural roads; a lot of concrete Jersey barrier on the dense motorway network (Bandeirantes, Dutra, Imigrantes).
road_furniture.line_paint: Yellow centre line with white edge lines; yellow-on-black hazard chevrons.
road_furniture.curb_style: Painted black-and-white or yellow kerbs common throughout the cities.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: The national ladder-and-holes concrete pole. Very dense Petrobras/Ipiranga and Itaú branding; toll plazas frequent on the private highways.

architecture.roof_style: Low-pitched gables in towns; flat concrete slabs on apartment blocks and self-built housing.
architecture.roof_material: Terracotta tile, with fibre-cement and concrete slabs on newer builds.
architecture.wall_construction: Plastered painted masonry in wealthier areas; extensive bare-brick self-built housing on the urban periphery.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Bare brick, whitewash, and bright colours; grey concrete high-rises.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Favelas stacked up steep hillsides in Rio and São Paulo; dense high-rise skylines; Baroque colonial towns in Minas Gerais (Ouro Preto, Tiradentes); coffee-farm houses (fazendas).

nature.vegetation: Atlantic Forest (Mata Atlântica) on the coastal ranges; heavily cleared interior with pasture, sugarcane, eucalyptus plantations and — in Minas and Espírito Santo — coffee plantations.
nature.terrain: Hilly. The Serra do Mar coastal escarpment rises abruptly behind a narrow coastal plain; the interior is rolling plateau cut by the Paraíba and Paraná valleys.
nature.climate_signature: Humid subtropical to tropical, with a warm wet summer and a drier, milder winter. Strong, deep reddish-orange roadside soil is a classic tell for this region and the adjoining centre-west.

vehicles.plate_color: Mercosur white plate with a blue 'BRASIL' strip; older grey plates still common; red plates on taxis, buses and trucks.
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: The full national mix plus heavier traffic — buses, trucks and app cars in the metros. Motorcycle couriers common in the cities.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Mostly Gen 3 and Gen 4; some older Gen 2.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: The best-covered part of Brazil by far — dense in every city and along the whole road network, mostly white car.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same language, plates, poles and Atlantic Forest on the coast
confusion_set.tiebreaker: The Southeast is warmer, has hillside favelas and big tropical cities, and no araucaria pines or German/Italian colonial architecture; the South is cooler and European-settled.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Identical red soil, pasture and eucalyptus, same infrastructure
confusion_set.tiebreaker: The Centre-West is flatter Cerrado with vast soy/cattle farms and thinner coverage; the Southeast has mountains (Serra do Mar), coast and dense population.
The Northeast interior is dry Caatinga scrub with pale soil and poorer roads; the Southeast is green, hilly and developed with red soil.
